items.title: Repository change reviewer
items.description: Review a Git diff and keep findings tied to added lines.
items.scenario: A checkout calculation changes multiplication to addition. The reviewer flags the changed line and suggests a correction.
steps: Parse added-line locations from a unified Git diff.
Ask for structured findings with reasons and suggested fixes.
Separate findings with valid locations from invented locations.
items.failure: Change the fixture finding to an unknown path or line. It moves to rejected_locations rather than appearing as an accepted finding. Restore the original response to recover.
items.adapt: Replace input.json.diff with the output of git diff --no-ext-diff --unified=3. Keep the review local until a person checks it. This parser covers ordinary text diffs, not combined merge diffs or binary patches.
items.limits: Location checks establish where a finding points. A person must still judge whether the bug and suggested fix are correct.

items.title: Support ticket triage
items.description: Classify a ticket and draft a reply for a person to review.
items.scenario: A customer reports a duplicate charge. The output includes a billing category, invoice ID and unsent reply.
steps: Read the ticket and request a constrained category and priority.
Retry an invalid response within a two-request limit.
Check that the extracted invoice occurs in the ticket; save an unsent draft.
items.failure: The first authored response is invalid JSON. The second is valid, so the report records two attempts. Replace both with invalid text to reach failure.json; restore the responses to recover.
items.adapt: Replace input.json with a ticket from your own queue and adjust schema.json categories. Review the draft and billing facts before sending anything. The application has no sending integration.
items.limits: Schema validation cannot guarantee that a reply is appropriate or that its promises are true. The output remains awaiting_human_review.

items.title: Document extraction pipeline
items.description: Turn invoice text into a validated record with source evidence.
items.scenario: An invoice includes an amount and currency but no due date. The result preserves the missing field instead of filling it in.
steps: Extract a record under a JSON schema.
Require the invoice ID and amount evidence to occur in the source text.
Report missing fields for a person to resolve.
items.failure: Change the returned amount to 999 while leaving its evidence unchanged. The grounding check stops the run. Restore the fixture and rerun; the result again reports the absent due date.
items.adapt: Replace input.json.text with extracted document text and change the schema and grounding checks together. This example starts with text; PDF OCR and image extraction are separate steps.
items.limits: Substring evidence checks are intentionally small and inspectable. Repeated amounts and ambiguous invoices need stronger field-to-span validation and human review.

items.title: Research assistant with citations
items.description: Answer from a supplied document collection and retain exact quotes.
items.scenario: A handbook states how long backups are retained. The assistant retrieves that passage and cites its source ID.
steps: Retrieve documents that match the supplied search terms.
Ask the model to answer only from those documents.
Check citation IDs and exact quotes against retrieved text.
items.failure: Set input.json.terms to an unmatched word. The application returns insufficient_evidence without calling a model. Restore the terms to recover. An invented citation quote is also rejected.
items.adapt: Replace the documents and query terms in input.json. The retriever uses simple lexical matching; replace that step with ranked retrieval when the collection grows.
items.limits: An exact quote proves that text exists, not that it supports every claim in an answer. The result is marked needs_review; check the claim-to-citation relationship.

items.title: Resumable batch processor
items.description: Classify records, save checkpoints and continue after interruption.
items.scenario: Three support records produce billing, account and technical labels. Completed record IDs survive a stopped process.
steps: Check that IDs are unique and the input matches any saved checkpoint.
Request and validate one unfinished record at a time.
Write a complete checkpoint and rename it before moving to the next record.
items.failure: Run KUJO_STOP_AFTER=1 kujo run main.kujo. Exit code 3 means the first result was saved. Run again without that variable to finish; the first request is skipped.
items.adapt: Replace input.json.records with your batch. Live mode can process additional IDs without fixture files. Use a fresh directory when changing the input, schema or prompt. Run one worker per checkpoint directory.
items.limits: This is a single-process checkpoint pattern, not a distributed queue or a power-loss durability guarantee. A request interrupted before its checkpoint may be repeated.

items.title: Safe tool-using assistant
items.description: Preview a proposed file edit and apply only the approved contents.
items.scenario: The assistant proposes a clearer heading for a local draft. Its first run writes a preview and leaves the draft untouched.
steps: Ask for complete before and after text for the allowed file.
Validate the path and original contents, then save a proposal and preview.
Require the printed proposal hash and unchanged source before applying.
items.failure: Run the printed apply command with a wrong hash, or edit draft.txt after preview. The application refuses to apply. Generate a new preview and review it before approving its new hash.
items.adapt: Start in the extracted bundle directory, which includes a disposable draft.txt. Adapt the allowed path and content checks deliberately. Never pass the model output to a shell. preview.diff is a human before/after display, not an apply-ready patch.
items.limits: Approval is a content check, not an operating-system sandbox. Use a trusted local directory with a regular draft.txt and no concurrent writers. For hostile workspaces, use filesystem isolation and race-resistant file operations.

items.title: Prompt regression lab
items.description: Compare prompt revisions against saved, labeled cases.
items.scenario: A baseline misclassifies a password-reset ticket. A more specific candidate passes both saved cases in the authored offline fixture.
steps: Run both prompts over the same labeled cases.
Record predictions, per-case correctness and prompt hashes.
Exit with a failed gate if the candidate passes fewer cases.
items.failure: Change both candidate response fixtures to technical. The candidate regresses and exits 4. Restore the original fixtures and rerun to recover.
items.adapt: Add representative cases and expected labels to input.json. Use live mode to collect actual model results, repeat runs and review errors before changing a production prompt.
items.limits: The offline score tests the evaluation machinery with authored responses. Two cases are not evidence of general prompt quality. Live results may vary even with temperature zero.

items.title: Provider fallback workflow
items.description: Try a second provider within a bounded request budget.
items.scenario: The primary response fails validation. The backup returns a usable classification and the report records both attempts.
steps: Try the configured primary once with a two-second timeout.
Treat transport errors and schema failures as unsuccessful attempts.
Try the backup once, then stop and save the routing trace.
items.failure: The primary fixture is invalid by design. Make the backup invalid too to exhaust the two-request budget and exit 2. Restore the backup fixture to recover. Tests also exercise a real local HTTP timeout.
items.adapt: Configure primary and backup endpoint, model and key variables independently. Use providers that accept the OpenAI-compatible chat format. Tune timeout and output-token limits in common.kujo for your workload.
items.limits: The budget limits request count and per-request output tokens, not dollar spend. A timed-out provider may still complete and charge for a request. No unbounded retries or automatic provider discovery are performed.
